question: Is explicit reasoning-chain text supervision of an LLM for multi-hop KGQA already standard, or do prior path-based methods only use latent paths and graph modules?
description: The reduction of the chain arm to prior art depends on how prior path-based methods supervise: MHGRN uses a graph relation network over subgraphs and Variational Reasoning uses latent paths from QA pairs, whereas the revised idea would explicitly supervise an LLM with chain text. If explicit chain-text instruction supervision for multi-hop KGQA is already standard, even the chain arm is fully covered; if it is not, there is a modest implementation-level delta that should still not be presented as a mechanism contribution.
rationale: This determines how much of even the chain arm is prior art and therefore whether any implementation-level residue can be claimed; the retrieved path-based works use latent or modular paths rather than explicit chain-text supervision, but coverage of this specific training format was not established.
